input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for the past few hours. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again so I can send photos to my family. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps! What do I need to do next?

I just checked my phone, and I see that I have a strong signal and it says 5G at the top, but there’s a little icon that looks like mobile data is turned off. I’m not sure about browsing the internet when not on Wi-Fi—I mostly just use my phone for calls and texts. 

I can make regular calls and send normal text messages without any trouble. What should I do next?

Okay, I turned on the mobile data like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose anything important if we keep trying different things?

I checked my APN settings, and it looks like there’s something called “internet” listed, but I don’t see anything set for the MMSC URL. I’m not really sure what any of that means—does that sound right, or is something missing?

I’m a bit nervous about resetting things—will this mess up anything else on my phone? And if I restart my phone, will I lose my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you please reassure me before we go ahead?

Alright, I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to restart my phone now—just to double-check, this won’t erase any of my photos or messages, right? I’m still a little anxious about that.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—this seems harder than I expected.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is turned off on my phone. What should I try next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it already has access to SMS, storage, and phone. Is there something else that could be causing the problem?

Oh, I see! I didn’t realize I’d used up all my data. I don’t want to change my plan, but I’d be willing to add more data if that will fix the problem. Could I please add 2GB? And just to be sure, it’s $4.00 total for 2GB, right? I’d like to go ahead with that if it will help me send my pictures again.

I tried sending a picture message again after adding the 2GB of data, but it still isn’t working. I even restarted my phone just in case, but I’m still having trouble. Is there anything else we can try?

I checked my network mode, and it’s set to prefer 4G and 5G, just like you said. But when I tried to run a speed test on my mobile data, it said there’s no connection. Does that mean something is still wrong with my data, even though I added more? What should I do next?

I reseated my SIM card and restarted my phone like you suggested, but I still can’t send picture messages, and the speed test still says there’s no connection. I’m really not sure what else to do—can you help me figure out what’s going on?
I haven’t received a payment request yet. Could you please send it to me? If paying the bill will help fix this, I’d like to get it sorted out as soon as possible.

I’ve paid my bill as requested, but I still can’t send picture messages, and my phone still says there’s no data connection. Is there anything else we can try, or do I need to wait a bit longer for the payment to go through? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all of this.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

It sounds like your mobile data might be turned off, which is required for sending and receiving MMS (picture messages). To fix this, please turn on your mobile data. 

Here’s what you need to do:
1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Find the option for “Mobile Data” or “Cellular Data.”

Next, let’s check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS problems. Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if you see anything unusual, or if you’re not sure how to check them, I can guide you through the process.

Thank you for checking. The MMSC URL is required for sending and receiving MMS, so if it’s missing, that’s likely the cause of your issue.

To fix this, you’ll need to reset your APN settings to the default values. This is a safe process and won’t delete any of your personal data or messages.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings? After resetting, you’ll also need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Let me know if you’re ready to proceed!

I understand your concerns, and I want to reassure you:

- Resetting your APN settings will only restore your phone’s network connection settings (like how your phone connects to the internet and sends MMS) to their default values. It will not affect your photos, messages, contacts, apps, or any other personal data.
- Restarting your phone after resetting the APN settings is just like turning it off and on again. This also will not delete or change any of your personal information.

These steps are safe and commonly used to fix issues like the one you’re experiencing. If you’re ready, I can guide you through resetting your APN settings and restarting your phone. Would you like to proceed?
